body:
olivia: hey team — customer reported streaming stopped mid-response when they switched from cellular -> WiFi. got partial output, client never resumed. request id: req_9b2f, conn id: conn-83. reproducible on their device (iPhone 12, RN WebView).

olivia: repro steps:
1) start a generation via SSE/fetch
2) while streaming, toggle from 4G -> WiFi
3) stream stops sending further chunks, client shows net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET and no close event, no automatic reconnect

maya: thanks, can you paste the client code and the exact error from the device console?

olivia: using fetch + ReadableStream in a React Native WebView. gist of client:
```
const res = await fetch('/v1/stream', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt })
});
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while (true) {
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  handleChunk(value);
}
```

maya: ok, pulled our logs for req_9b2f — we see a sequence: connection established, a few chunk flushes, then `upstream connection closed by client` at 15:27:11, then no 5xx from the backend. seems like the client or an intermediate NAT/edge closed the TCP.

maya: can you confirm whether the app is using HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2? and is there any proxy/VPN on the device?

olivia: HTTP/1.1 from the WebView. no VPN. customer says it happens when they leave home cell coverage and the phone autoconnects to WiFi (carrier handoff).

raj: adding eng-runtime. my hypothesis: source IP changes during the mobile->wifi switch, the LB sees the different 5-tuple and tears the connection. SSE over HTTP long-poll isn't resilient to IP changes.

daniel: agrees — typical NAT mapping change. load balancer will drop existing connections when client IP changes. depending on the client stack, you might not get a socket error; RN WebView sometimes silently cancels the fetch.

olivia: important detail: the reader.read() promise neither resolves nor rejects after the switch — it just hangs. console shows net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET followed by nothing. no onerror handler fired in app code.

maya: short-term mitigation suggestions for customer:
- implement application-level heartbeat detection: if no chunk for N seconds, abort and reconnect (client-side timeout).
- add server-side event IDs so client can resume from last-id on reconnect (id:value SSE events).
- consider switching to WebSocket for very mobile-heavy apps if reconnection/resume is critical.

raj: long-term for platform: consider default keepalive pings between CDN/LB and backend and send periodic comment lines from server (`:keepalive

`) every 15s so mobile stacks notice liveness. also add documented recommended client reconnection pattern and resume token.

daniel: I'll open an ops ticket to validate LB behavior on client IP changes and whether we can tune idle/keepalive for mobile flows. also check if our edge closes connections with 0-length FIN or RST on 5-tuple change.

olivia: customer also worried about billing — they saw partial tokens billed and want to know if a retry will double-charge.

maya: answered: billed tokens correspond to what was consumed server-side; if client reconnects and resumes from last event-id, they won't re-bill for already-generated tokens. we'll document resume flow for customers to avoid duplicate billing.

raj: action items (INF-2316):
1) eng-runtime: confirm LB/edge behavior on IP change and whether keepalive pings can be adjusted.
2) eng-runtime: prototype sending SSE comment keepalives and server-side `id` events to support resume.
3) docs: KB with sample client timeout + reconnect + resume snippet for RN/fetch and EventSource.
4) support: send recommended workaround to affected customers (heartbeat + reconnect).

deploy-bot: created INF-2316 and assigned to eng-runtime (https://redwood.internal/INF-2316).

maya: assigning priority=medium (intermittent, mobile-specific). @raj @daniel please confirm ETA and whether Dedicated/Dedicated Private customers need config knobs.

raj: will investigate today, update ticket with findings by EOD. planning note: keepalive default 15s seems safe but need to validate across cloud providers.

olivia: attaching device console snippet: `net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` + `TypeError: Cannot read property 'value' of undefined` when app tries to parse chunk. customer wants an ETA before Monday.

maya: noted, we'll push a KB and an interim workaround to the customer (client heartbeat + reconnect logic). following up in INF-2316. :thumbsup:
